listenings.text: Quick note to myself after that review call, before I forget it. The most expensive five words in that room were not a number. They were: I will check and come back. Every time somebody says that, the meeting stops, the decision waits another week, and the same question gets asked again by somebody more senior. And here is the thing. I am not asking anybody to guess, and I am certainly not asking anybody to know every number by heart. Nobody does. What I am asking for is the third answer, the one almost nobody gives. Say what you do know. Say which part you are not sure about. And then give me a time when you will confirm it. Three sentences. That is the difference between a decision made today and a decision made in October.

When I ask somebody where a number comes from, most people start with the detail and work forwards. They tell me about the invoice, then the supplier, then the contract, and four sentences later I still do not know where the explanation is going. I want it in the opposite order, and I want it in three sentences. First, what the number is. Second, what caused it. Third, whether it happens again. That is it. And here is a small test you can run on yourself before you speak. If your second sentence does not contain the word because, or something doing the same job as because, then the explanation has not started yet. You have only repeated the number in more words.
